resolved_issues.title: Missing values for required options wrongly get value of next option name
resolved_issues.body:
``` 
calRTT [options]

       --times <num>        "Times desc"
       --verbose            "if verbose"
```
For example, my CLI name is calRTT and it has two arguments, `times` and `verbose`. If I run this program in terminal and input as
`calRTT --times --verbose`, it will return string "--verbose" if I call `options.times`. But what I want is to throw an exception as it missed value **num**, instead of return the name of next option name with quotes. How can I solve this?

currently my code is:
```
const program = new Command()
program
.name("calRTT")
.option('-t, --times', 'Times desc')
.option('-v, --verbose' 'if verbose')

program.parse(process.argv)
const options = program.opts()
```

resolved_issues.title: Required non-option arguments only checked with .action()?
resolved_issues.body:
It appears that `commander@7.2.0` only checks `.arguments()` for the top-level command if `.action()` is given.  For example:

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
const { Command } = require('commander');
const command = new Command();
command
  .arguments('<source>')
  .allowExcessArguments(false)
  .description('do something with a single source file')
  .action(() => {});
command.parse();
console.log('Called with arguments:', command.args);
```

Has the following behavior

    $ ./example.js
    error: missing required argument 'source'
    $ ./example.js one
    Called with arguments: [ 'one' ]
    $ ./example.js one two
    error: too many arguments. Expected 1 argument but got 2.

If `.action(() => {});` is commented out, it has the following behavior:

    $ ./example.js 
    Called with arguments: []
    $ ./example.js one
    Called with arguments: [ 'one' ]
    $ ./example.js one two
    Called with arguments: [ 'one', 'two' ]

Which was surprising to me.  If this is intentional, perhaps a comment could be added to the [Specify the argument syntax section of `Readme.md`](https://github.com/tj/commander.js/blob/master/Readme.md#specify-the-argument-syntax) to warn users?  If not, perhaps it could be fixed?

Thanks for considering,
Kevin
